problem:
Title: Mills' Theorem

There exists a [[Definition:Real Number|real number]] $A$ such that $\floor {A^{3^n} }$ is a [[Definition:Prime Number|prime number]] for all $n \in \N_{>0}$, where:

:$\floor x$ denotes the [[Definition:Floor Function|floor function]] of $x$
:$\N$ denotes the [[Definition:Set|set]] of all [[Definition:Natural Number|natural numbers]].
